facts.title: Benzene spike on the Houston Ship Channel
facts.time_note: Monitor hours are CST as TCEQ publishes them; the company report uses local time (CDT, CST+1). TCEQ labels AutoGC data provisional and subject to change.

detection.rule: value >= max(10 x 7-day median baseline, 10 ppb)

checks.note: initial notice filed 2024-06-21T14:38 local, 5.0 h after the reported discovery 2024-06-21T09:38
final report dated 2024-07-03, 12 days after the event ended

cannot_say: A matching report is not proof the facility caused every reading; other sources can add to a spike.
'Not yet reported' is not a finding about any facility: Texas requires a report only at or above a reportable quantity, and air readings cannot measure how much was released (30 TAC 101.201).
The upwind corridor comes from wind direction at one monitor (geometry only), not a dispersion model; it cannot tell facilities along the same bearing apart.
Facility coordinates are as published by EPA ECHO and may be approximate.
Only regulator-grade monitors whose data the state publishes are used (including two industry-funded Houston Regional Monitoring sites), never low-cost sensors.
